newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia massacre victims get killer's assets.
newsitem.headline: Australia massacre victims get killer's assets.

text.p: More than A$1 million (US$740,000) in assets stripped from Australian mass killer Martin Bryant will be distributed to survivors of the Port Arthur massacre, the Tasmania state government said on Friday.
A court last year ordered Bryant to surrender his assets to assist survivors of the fatal shooting of 35 people at the Port Arthur historial site in the island state last April.
Tasmanian Attorney-General Ray Groom said eligible victims could expect payment by the end of December, although some money had already been given to people in financial hardship.
The fund stood at just under A$1.3 million, with some further assets still to be sold, Groom said.
Bryant, who never took a full-time job, inherited his wealth, including a large house, from a middle-aged woman who paid him to run errands before her death in 1992.
Last year's court ruling followed the Tasmanian parliament's approval of special legislation enabling prosecutors to seize Bryant's assets.
Bryant, 29, is serving a life sentence without parole.
